author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A close friend of Madeline “Amy” Sweeney is remembering the Massachusetts flight attendant’s courage aboard American Airlines Flight 11 on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks.

Sweeney was working the Boston-to-Los Angeles flight when it was hijacked after departing Logan Airport. Before the aircraft struck the World Trade Center’s North Tower, she contacted American Airlines and relayed critical information about what was happening aboard the plane.

Barbara Bowen, a fellow flight attendant and longtime friend, told WHDH that the two had built a friendship through years of trips and shared family milestones. Bowen had switched crews so she could be home when her son started school, leaving her away from Flight 11 that morning.

Massachusetts later created the Madeline Amy Sweeney Award for Civilian Bravery in her name. The annual honor recognizes people who show exceptional courage while trying to save another person’s life. Friday’s remembrance linked Sweeney’s final call to that continuing public legacy and to Boston’s central role in the history of the attacks.
dek: The Massachusetts flight attendant relayed crucial details about the hijacking before the plane struck the World Trade Center.
headline: Friend remembers Flight 11 attendant Amy Sweeney’s final act of courage
